raw_response:
I will still follow what worked for me last year, then adjust a little. My land is only 3 mu, so every bag of fertilizer costs real money, but if I cut fertilizer too hard and lose yield, that hurts more. In Quzhou with well water, I do not like to let wheat depend only on rain. Wheat is my steady crop, so I will feed it a bit heavier and water it about three times if the season is normal. Maize comes after wheat, and the stubble period is tight, so I will keep it simple and fast, usually no-tillage or direct seeding after harvest. I watch what farmers around me do, and most people here use improved wheat seed and hybrid maize, with fertilizer split between base and topdressing. On my small area, family labor is enough, so I will spend on seed, fertilizer, and a few pesticide sprays, not on fancy extras.

decision.reasoning_summary: I will farm this year much like last year because that is the safest way on 3 mu, but I will keep the inputs steady so I do not lose yield. For wheat, I will use improved seed, give enough nitrogen with some phosphorus and potassium, and use my well for three irrigations because wheat here cannot rely on rainfall alone. For maize, I will switch fast after wheat harvest, usually with no-tillage to save time and labor, and I will use hybrid seed with solid fertilizer and two irrigations. I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than watch the crop turn weak, but because my farm is small, I will keep pesticide sprays to what is needed and avoid wasting money on anything extra.
